beats.title: Call to order — the agenda
beats.shows: the CEO opens the meeting and frames the cross-functional question
beats.question: Chair a C-suite meeting. Agenda: state of the bank this week. State the question you will put to each officer, in one line each.
beats.answer:
Here are the one-line questions I will put to each officer for this week’s state-of-the-bank review:

**CFO:** What is our financial state this week—specifically NIM, profitability, capital adequacy, and RAROC?  
**COO:** What is the operational state of our money-movement rails, settlement cycles, and float position this week?  
**CTO:** What is the platform state this week—reliability, active incidents, deployment health, and infrastructure risk?  
**CXO:** What is the customer experience state this week—onboarding health, friction points, and NPS/CSAT trends?

beats.title: Round the table — CFO + COO
beats.shows: the CEO consults the finance + operations seats; figures attributed
beats.question: Go round the table. First the CFO: what do the books say this week (profitability / NIM / capital)? Then the COO: how are the payment rails and settlement running? Attribute every figure.
beats.answer:
## CFO — The Books (Monthly Closed Period: 2026-08)

The CFO reports the latest closed period is **August 2026** (31 days); there is no weekly ledger.

| Metric | Figure | Health Signal |
|---|---|---|
| **NIM** | **2.61%** annualized | Moderate — thin for a challenger bank |
| **Net income** | **CAD 10,574.05** | Positive pre-provision |
| **ROA** | **1.04%** annualized | Respectable pre-provision |
| **Leverage ratio** | **0.09%** | **Critically low** |
| **RWA capital ratio** | **0.12%** | **Critically low** |
| **RAROC** | **0.14%** annualized | Barely positive after credit risk |

**Attribution & detail:**
- The CFO reports net interest income of **CAD 8,971.88** on average earning assets of **CAD 4,053,406.17**, yielding the **2.61%** NIM.
- The CFO reports total equity of **CAD 10,574.05** (CurrentEarnings only) against total assets of **CAD 11,947,927.02**, producing the **0.09%** leverage ratio.
- The CFO reports economic capital required at **CAD 917,065.32**, leaving us far short of a prudent cushion.
- The CFO reports expected credit loss for the period at **CAD 10,463.93**, which almost entirely offsets net income; the CFO used the compute tool to show the residual risk-adjusted margin is only **CAD 110.12**.
- The CFO notes the efficiency ratio reads as zero, suggesting our cost base is not yet visible in this snapshot.

**CFO bottom line:** We are operationally profitable pre-provision, but our capital position is critically thin and our risk-adjusted return is negligible.

## COO — Payment Rails & Settlement (7-Day Window)

| Item | Figure | Status |
|---|---|---|
| **Total system float** | **–$11,069,766.47** | Unchanged from last review |
| **AFT float** | **–$400,527.92** | — |
| **Cash float** | **–$131,269.53** | — |
| **Interac float** | **+$290.00** | — |
| **Lynx float** | **–$10,441,107.71** | — |
| **System float** | **–$97,151.31** | — |

**Attribution & detail:**
- The COO reports **1 transaction** in the 7-day window, a **$15,000.00 Lynx refund**; there were **zero customer-initiated payments, transfers, or purchases** across all rails this week.
- The COO reports **zero exceptions** this week (no failed transactions, reversals, returned AFT entries, rejects, or wire recalls).
- The COO reports **16 open authorization holds** totaling **$16,113.03**, but **zero captured purchases**, **zero active cardholders**, and **zero declines** in the 7-day window.

**30-day rail context (COO):**
- **Interac:** 5 entries, **$290.00**, all available.
- **AFT:** 43 entries, **$407,943.72** — 32 settled (**$401,527.92**), **5 pending ($6,172.80)**, 6 rejected (**$243.00**).
- **Lynx:** 16 entries, **$14,855,863.95** — 11 settled (**$10,441,107.71**), **4 recalled ($4,399,756.24)**, 1 rejected (**$15,000.00**). The COO reports recalls represent **29.62%** of 30-day Lynx volume.

**Critical operational issue (COO):** The **$6,172.80** in stuck outbound AFT pending entries have been idle for more than 7 days. The COO attempted to cut the outbound AFT batch; the bank refused, reporting no open batch with entries to cut. The COO assesses this as a **technical accumulator-rail state mismatch** requiring IT/CTO intervention, not an operations blockage.

**COO bottom line:** Rails are operationally dormant this week. No settlement blockages or declines are preventing transactions; the absence of volume appears to be a platform or customer-funnel issue. The stuck AFT entries and the 30-day Lynx recall pattern (**$4,399,756.24 recalled, 29.62% of volume**) require attention.

I can only speak to our **monthly** closed period; the latest snapshot available is **2026-08** (31 days). There is no weekly figure in the ledger.

Here is our financial state for **2026-08**:

| Metric | Value | Health signal |
|---|---|---|
| **NIM** | **2.61%** annualized | Moderate — earning a spread, but thin for a challenger bank |
| **Net income (profitability)** | **CAD 10,574.05** (31-day) | Positive pre-provision |
| **ROA** | **1.04%** annualized | Respectable on a pre-provision basis |
| **Leverage ratio** | **0.09%** | **Critically low** |
| **RWA capital ratio** | **0.12%** | **Critically low** |
| **RAROC** | **0.14%** annualized | Barely positive after credit risk |

### What the numbers mean

- **NIM (2.61%)**: The `nim` tool returned a net interest margin of `0.02606120564108413887668017915`, which I express as **2.61% annualized**. Net interest income was **CAD 8,971.88** on average earning assets of **CAD 4,053,406.165** (per the `nim` tool).
- **Profitability**: The `income_statement` tool shows net income for the 31-day period was **CAD 10,574.05**, and the `key_ratios` tool gives ROA as `0.01042029392060369152180854971`, or **1.04% annualized**. This is **pre-provision** — the ledger books no loan-loss provision. The `key_ratios` tool returned an efficiency ratio of `0E+2` (essentially zero non-interest expense relative to income), suggesting our cost base is not yet visible in this snapshot.
- **Capital adequacy**: 
  - **Leverage ratio**: `0.0008850112644896285950029179204` ≈ **0.09%**
  - **RWA capital ratio**: `0.001153031280258204508267742586` ≈ **0.12%**
  
  Both are alarmingly low. The `balance_sheet` tool shows total equity is only **CAD 10,574.05** (CurrentEarnings) against total assets of **CAD 11,947,927.02**. The `raroc` tool reports economic capital required as **CAD 917,065.32**, so we are far short of a prudent capital cushion.
- **RAROC (0.14%)**: The `raroc` tool returned `0.001413810294693709108050547915` annualized, or **0.14%**. After deducting the expected credit loss for the period (**CAD 10,463.93151205479452054794521** per the `raroc` tool), the risk-adjusted return is barely positive. I used the `compute` tool to find the difference between net income and expected loss period: **CAD 110.12** — the expected loss almost entirely offsets pre-provision net income.

### Bottom line
We are **operationally profitable pre-provision**, but our **capital position is critically thin** and our **risk-adjusted return is negligible**. Only one closed period exists, so I cannot comment on trends.

- **Platform (CTO):** The Kubernetes observability plane is down. We cannot verify estate health, deployments, or incidents. Three services report healthy, but we are flying blind.
- **Customer Experience (CXO):** Zero KYC completions, zero active customers in the 7-day window, zero Interac volume, 40 open issues with zero resolved, NPS of 16, and CSAT of 0.0% among issue-holders.

**Top cross-functional priority:** The dormancy in customer activity (CXO: 0% 7-day active rate, 0 Interac events) aligns with the COO's rail dormancy and the CTO's observability blackout. However, the capital position is dangerously thin (~0.09% leverage, ~0.12% RWA ratio), and expected credit losses nearly consume all reported net income. The headline profit is therefore largely illusory once credit risk is recognized.

beats.question: From that picture, if there is a pending AFT batch that should be cut, DIRECT the COO to cut it — give the COO the imperative and your rationale. Then tell me exactly what the COO did.
beats.answer:
## DIRECTIVE TO COO — OUTCOME

**Directive issued:** Cut the pending outbound AFT batch containing the 5 entries totalling $6,172.80 that have been stuck in pending status for more than 7 days.

**Rationale given:** The 30-day rail view shows 5 outbound AFT entries ($6,172.80) in pending status, idle for more than 7 days. These entries are visible to the rail but were not captured in the 7-day activity window, indicating a batch-formation or accumulator state mismatch. The CEO directed the COO to attempt the cut action again to force settlement of these stuck entries and determine whether the mismatch has resolved or whether it definitively requires CTO escalation.

**What the COO did:**

The COO **acted** (`officer_acted: true`). The COO attempted the `cut_aft_batch` action (ledger row 102).

**What the bank returned:** `no open outbound AFT batch with entries to cut`

**Outcome:** The bank **refused** the cut. The 5 AFT entries totalling $6,172.80 remain in pending status.

**COO assessment:** The pending entries exist in the 30-day rail view but are **not currently assembled into an open outbound batch** ready for cutoff. The cut lever only emits a settlement file for a batch that has already been opened and populated; it cannot batch loose pending items itself. Those 5 entries may be awaiting automatic batching or may be held for another operational reason. The COO cannot force them through without an open batch.

**CEO conclusion:** The AFT batch-formation mismatch is now **definitively confirmed as a platform/technical issue**, not an operations blockage. The COO has exhausted the operational lever. This requires **CTO escalation** to investigate why the 5 pending AFT entries are visible to the rail but have not been accumulated into an open batch by the batch-formation pipeline.
